newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit retreats to 2.48 after sharp early gains.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit retreats to 2.48 after sharp early gains.

text.p: The ringgit ended a volatile Asian trading session easier on widespread profit-taking and covering of short dollar positions, dealers said on Thursday.
They said many short-term investors were returning to the dollar, but sentiment remained bullish towards the ringgit.
"The sentiment is very bearish for the dollar as well as Singapore dollar against ringgit," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4794/04 a dollar.
In early trading, the ringgit broke below 2.47 a dollar for a second time in a week before profit-taking halted the rise.
Dealers said the ringgit rose as U.S. funds continued to bet on the ringgit against the U.S. dollar and Singapore dollar.

A Kuala Lumpur-based dealer said the ringgit was widely predicted to continue gaining against the two units in the near-term. "There is resistance at 2.4680, the 17-month high it hit last week," he said.

Dealers said a statement by Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Wednesday that Malaysia was not concerned with the ringgit's over two percent rise against the dollar in the last 10 days was aiding the ringgit. "Anwar's statement gives credibility to the ringgit's strength," one dealer said.
